ic_name: MIPI SPMI v2.0 + RFFE v3.0 (System Power Management + RF Front-End Control)
opcode_synthesis_skipped_reason: L2.protocol_overview.half_duplex is not True and no explicit opcode/command-table heading was found in input/docs/. Free-form hex bytes in prose, SVG labels, or PDF text do not constitute opcode evidence.
protocol_type: MIPI two-wire command-frame protocol. Each transaction is SSC -> Command Frame (+parity) -> [Address Frame (+parity)] -> [Data Frame(s) (+parity)] -> Bus Park Cycle. The Command Frame's top bits select the slave (SLAVE_ID for SPMI, USID/GSID for RFFE) and the low bits select the command (or, for Register 0 Write, carry 7 data bits). All bits are MSB-first.

channels.name: SCLK
channels.description: Serial clock supplied by the active master; idles low; up to 26 MHz (SPMI / RFFE v1-v2) or 52 MHz (RFFE v3.0).

channels.name: SDATA
channels.description: Serial data carrying command/address/data frames MSB-first, each with an odd parity bit; turned around within a transaction; idles low.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: Per-byte handshake: receiver pulls SDA LOW during the 9th SCL clock pulse to ACK; leaves HIGH to NACK.
Optional clock-stretching handshake: slave holds SCL LOW after a byte to delay the next byte.
There is no AMBA-style per-cycle VALID/READY; the handshake is byte-level + bit-level via SCL synchronization.

transaction_framing.start_S: HIGH-to-LOW transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.stop_P: LOW-to-HIGH transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH
transaction_framing.repeated_start_Sr: Functionally identical to S; keeps bus busy without an intervening STOP
transaction_framing.byte: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock pulse = 9 SCL cycles
transaction_framing.ack_bit: Receiver pulls SDA LOW during 9th SCL clock pulse
transaction_framing.nack_bit: SDA remains HIGH during 9th SCL clock pulse

address_byte_format.bits_0_to_7: 7-bit slave address (LSB-first into ADDRESS field, MSB-first on wire)
address_byte_format.bit_8: R/W direction bit; 0 = write to slave; 1 = read from slave
address_byte_format.10_bit_addressing: Two address bytes: first byte 0b11110XX0/1 (XX = upper 2 address bits + R/W); second byte = lower 8 address bits

single_response_for_write: Every byte (including the address byte) is acknowledged by the receiver via an ACK / NACK on the 9th clock pulse.
per_beat_response_for_read: Each read byte gets an ACK from the master-receiver, except the last byte where master sends NACK to signal end of transfer.

rows: Reserved for future purposes including Device ID

master_to_slave_write_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=0 → ACK → DATA0 → ACK → DATA1 → ACK → … → P
Optional repeated START between bytes: S … DATA → ACK → Sr → SLAVE_ADDR2 || R/W → …
slave_to_master_read_transaction: S → SLAVE_ADDR[7:1] || R/W=1 → ACK (slave) → DATA0 (slave drives SDA) → ACK (master) → DATA1 → ACK → … → DATAN → NACK (master) → P

frame_types.name: Sequence Start Condition (SSC)
frame_types.description: A defined SDATA pulse while SCLK is low that starts every transaction and synchronizes all devices.

frame_types.name: Command Frame
frame_types.description: Slave identifier (SLAVE_ID / USID-GSID) + command opcode, MSB-first, + odd parity. Register 0 Write carries 7 data bits here.

frame_types.name: Address Frame
frame_types.description: 8-bit (standard) or 16-bit (Extended Long) register address, MSB-first, + odd parity.

frame_types.name: Data Frame
frame_types.description: 8 data bits MSB-first + odd parity; Extended/Long commands carry a byte count so the number of data frames is explicit.

frame_types.name: Bus Park Cycle
frame_types.description: Terminates the transaction and returns the bus to idle (SCLK toggling, SDATA released).

rffe_commands: Interrupt Read / Interrupt Identification and Clearing

rffe_command_details.name: Interrupt Read / Interrupt Identification and Clearing

addressing.rffe: 4-bit USID + 4-bit GSID (group); broadcast USID = all slaves
addressing.register_0: special low-overhead register; Register 0 Write carries 7 data bits in the command frame.

frame_format.parity: each frame ends with one odd parity bit.
frame_format.transaction_framing: SSC, then Command Frame, then optional Address Frame and Data Frame(s), then Bus Park Cycle.
frame_format.no_i2c_start_stop: Framing is by SSC + Bus Park Cycle, NOT an I2C START (SDA falling while SCL high) / STOP condition.
